tips.title: Use 0.6mm Acrylic Sheets for Precision
tips.text: For detailed scale model builds, opt for 0.6mm thick acrylic sheets from brands like **Plexiglas** or **Lucite**. Their clarity and rigidity make them ideal for cutting intricate shapes with a **utility knife** and **razor blade**. Avoid thinner sheets as they are prone to warping.

tips.title: Apply 3M 776 Adhesive for Strong Bonds
tips.text: Use **3M 776 Contact Adhesive** for bonding plastic sheets. It provides a strong, permanent bond without leaving residue. Apply a thin layer to both surfaces, press together, and allow 24 hours to cure for maximum strength.

Before gluing, prime plastic surfaces with a **polypropylene primer** like **Plasti-Kote**. This enhances adhesion, especially with **cyanoacrylate (CA)** glue. Prime the surface thoroughly, let it dry, then apply glue for a durable bond.

tips.title: Source from Specialty Model Shops
tips.text: Purchase materials from **modeling specialty stores** like **Modelshop** or **Plastikar**. They offer **pre-cut plastic sheets**, **adhesives**, and **primers** tailored for scale modeling. These stores often provide expert advice on material compatibility.

tips.title: Store Sheets in Cool, Dry Containers
tips.text: Keep plastic sheets in **cool, dry containers** or **foam boxes** to prevent warping. Avoid direct sunlight and high humidity. **PVC sheets** should be stored separately from **acrylics** to prevent chemical reactions.
